caption: The hero's first push-off from standing, side-on: the rear boot now keeps its ball on the turf and lifts its heel instead of flicking its toes up; GL fallback lighting and ground speckle still fall short of Wukong.
Hero's first step from rest, side-on: the rear boot lifts its heel with the ball on the turf, no toe flick; boots still read as chunky clogs and the figure is flat-lit.
Hero settling after a walk stop: both boots flat and grounded; the face is still lost grey under the hood and the scene lacks Wukong-grade grading.
Hero mid-run stride on open turf by the cottage, rear 3/4 at 09:00; hat, capelet and staff read, but the boots are too small in frame to judge the heel-strike toe tip and the backlit robe is dark.
Gather step over ticks 0-20 (3-tick spacing): the boot now arrives at ticks 12-15 instead of snapping in by tick 9; rear lens, boots partly hidden by the robe.
Hero turning on the spot, the forward boot mid-way through its longer 0.26 s gather step; lens still reads from behind, not side-on, and the hero looks small against dark grass.

Turn on the spot side-on at ticks 0,4,8,12,16,20,30 with the harness fixed: the head reaches the lens first, the body follows, the gather boot sets down with no pop; the meadow is flat and dark at this scale and the robe hides the boots.
Tick 8 of the turn: the head already turned to the lens while the chest is still side-on; the staff, hat and capelet read, but the lighting is flat and the scene empty, not a Wukong frame yet.

Boot crops at ticks 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 of the turn: the gather boot lifts, travels in and sets down beside the pivot boot with no pop or slide; the boots sit in shadow, too dark to judge sole contact by eye.

Low side lens on the hero's left turn on the spot at tick 9: the forward boot is lifted mid-gather while the pivot boot stays planted; the bare turf (grass off for the lens) shows a harsh repeating dash texture.
Close crop of the climb at frame 16 (old spot): the hero sits in a ruined corner, one hand low near the hip instead of up on a hold.

Hero climbing the keep from behind at frame 18: the shot spot sits at a broken wall end, so the body hangs half past the face's edge with the left side in the air; the climb pose cannot be judged here.

Hero climbing the keep's outer face from behind on the new raycast-picked spot (intact 7.6 m stretch, both hands on stone); the stone shows speckle noise under the GL fallback and the hero's head reads large.
Three-quarter of the same climb: knee up on a course, hands reaching, valley beyond; framing now judges the move, but the stone texture is noisy and the shadow side of the face goes near-black.

Hero climbing the keep's outer face from behind (frame 22, sideways stops at a course end now ease in over ~1 s): stone and lighting read well, but both arms are hidden under the capelet instead of reaching up onto the stones.
Same climb 6 frames later, a course higher: the knees step up, but from behind the hands still never show above the shoulders, so the reach reads weak; the face's shadow side is near-black.
Same climb frame before (left, hanging 0.37 m off the wall, knee jutting) and after (right, hugging the wall); the GL renderer is flat-lit and the arms are hidden under the capelet.
Climbing frames f22/28/34: the body now hangs in close to the stones (shoulders 0.21 m off, was 0.37) with the stepping knee frogged out to the side; the hands still never rise above the shoulders.

Hero climbing the keep from behind after the overhead-reach change: the right arm now rises beside the head, but no hand clears the hat brim yet and the shaded side of the stones goes near-black under the GL fallback.
Climb frames f24/f27/f30 cropped: the right upper arm lifts toward the hat by f30 (before: hidden under the capelet), but from behind the reach still does not read as overhead.
Climb with the new shoulder shrug: the left forearm now shows over the capelet beside the hat, but the reach still stops at head height and the figure is small in frame.
Climbing the keep from a rear three-quarter: hero hangs close to the stones with a knee turned out, but the hands only reach the hat brim, never fully overhead.
Boss growth surge roar at size 3.0, front lens, BEFORE: a column of its own ring of fire stands dead ahead and hides the chest and roar.

Boss growth surge roar at size 2.8 AFTER: the ring of fire leaves a gap on its front so the roar with the left fist flung up reads; still no face, and its size does not read without the hero in frame.
Boss settling to guard at size 3.2 at the end of the surge, framed between two flames; clear silhouette, but the giant's scale and face still fall short of Wukong.

Climbing the keep from behind: the body now waits while a hand reaches, so the left fist is raised beside the hat; the climber also holds on through a hole in the face instead of dropping. Still wrong: the hand stops at the hat brim, never clearly overhead.
2x crop of the same frame: fist and forearm up at head height on the left; the right arm hidden by the capelet, stone shows GL-fallback speckle.

Surge frames st=46/52/56: roar, fist still raised as the settle starts, then both hands meet the haft at the chest as the glaive tips into guard; no hunched frame left, but fire columns still crowd the foreground.

Boss growth surge, front-lit at s~1.9: the knight now still roars with the left fist up where the old regrip had both fists closed round the visor (a hunch); face still hidden behind the helm slit, scale unreadable without the hero in frame.
Helm crops during the surge: before (blank helm, mid-roar), after mid-roar (slit blazing across the eyes) and after at the settle; the slit reads as one bar, the two eye hot points barely separate.

The boss settling after its growth roar (size 3.2): the helm's sight slit now burns with the ember instead of reading as a blank face; the ring-of-fire columns still fill a third of the frame and the hero is not in shot for scale.

The boss settling after its growth roar (size 3.2) with the hero standing beside it for scale (about 3x the hero); the ring of fire has burned down to embers and its thinned smoke no longer hides the helm. Still: the ember tongues read as thin streaks and the hero is small at this lens.

The growth roar (size 3.2) from the front with the hero in frame; the ring-of-fire columns now age correctly in the shot and are fading red tongues by the roar instead of full-height columns filling a third of the frame.
The boss at its phase-1 size (2.2) on its post with the hero 2.5 m in front for scale; it reads about twice the hero, but the turf is bare dark mud and the knight's face is in shadow.

Phase-3 final size (4.6) beside the hero after the second growth surge, the cloudless polygon overhead now fixed; the hero is lost in dust at its boot and a flat pale low-poly sprig fills the foreground.
Ring of fire during the roar, before (left) and after (right): the ring's tongues now fade out early and shrink instead of standing as thin red streaks; smoke still reads muddy.

Seeding grass panicle close to the lens, before (left: flat pale 4-vertex diamonds) and after (right: folded husks with a keel, veins, pale margins and a dark base); the flowering stems are still wide flat ribbons up close.
Knee-height lens in the dry meadow with the new spikelet husks in the foreground; the grass reads as real seeding grass, but the near blades are still over-saturated straw-yellow.
Ring floor crop, before (top: dark brown mud with pale flakes) and after (bottom: cool grey ash drifts with char patches and stubble).

The boss ring's floor at the phase-2 settle now reads as grey wood-ash over black char instead of brown mud; still wrong: the cinder speckle is too even and the hero is half-hidden in the knight's boot dust.

Phase-2 settle beside the hero: the noon sky is clear of the white spark 'stars' and the growth dust falls on the knight's flanks, not over the hero; still: the knight is seen from behind-quarter and its dust still rolls past its right boot.
Phase-3 final size after the second surge, no spark field; still wrong: loose orange fire tongues float high in the sky and a pale seeding-grass sprig fills the left foreground.
Same frame before (left: ~500 white ring-fire sparks hanging 8 m up like daytime stars, dust over the hero) and after (right: sparks cool and die low, sky clean).
Phase-3 boss settle (4.6x) after the shot-harness fix: no stray fire tongues in the sky, only the ring's smoke; still wrong: the pale flat seeding-grass sprig fills the left foreground.
Before/after: the 'fire tongues floating in the sky' were the shot harness re-emitting one-shot ring flames (left), not the game; fixed (right).

Phase-3 boss settle (4.6x) beside the hero: the cream seeding sprig no longer stands on the ring's ash lip, the edge clumps are singed short; still wrong: the ash floor speckle is even and the boss's face slit is small at this range.
Ring lip close-up, after (top) vs before (bottom): full-height cream seed heads on the burnt edge are gone, the singed band is shorter and browner.
Before (left, FX frozen at spawn) vs after (right, ember/grit/impact FX stepped with the boss): the boot dust has rolled on and embers have risen; the frozen version misrepresented the game.
Helm close lens mid-roar: the burning sight slit reads as one bar, the two eye hot points do not separate, and a grey streak runs down the helm; background mountain texture is stripy.

Phase-2 growth roar (st=56) with the seam embers now aged in the shot: cinders drift up round the helm instead of a frozen spit; the knight still shows its back to this lens and the ring floor speckle is too even.

Boss helm close-up mid-roar (phase-2 surge): the sight slit is now a thin dark-red cut with two separate white-hot eye points; still wrong: the keel ridge down the face reads as a fuzzy grey smoke streak.
Before (left): the slit burned as one white-clipped bar; after (right): a thin cut pinched at the keel with two round hot eyes.

Boss growth roar, helm lens: the keel is now a crisp narrow rubbed-steel ridge with sooted flanks between the two ember eyes; the mountain backdrop is still a flat procedural cone and the ember spits are dotty.
Helm close-up before (left: the keel smeared into a fuzzy grey smoke streak) and after (right: a hard forged line); the plate still reads a little plasticky in GL.
Ash floor foreground before (top: even dash speckle everywhere) and after (bottom: clean ash, cinders heaped in hollows and tussocks); the green stubble blades should be singed.

Phase-2 settle in the burnt ring: the ash floor is now smooth grey wood-ash with cinders and stumps clumped in patches instead of an even black pepper; bright green shoots still poke through the ash and the trees are blotchy in GL.
Boss ring at the phase-2 settle: the ash floor now carries only sparse char-black stubble with dead straw tips and no wildflowers; the trees still read soft and the knight faces away from the lens.
Foreground strip before (top: spring-green tufts and flower stems on the ash) and after (bottom: thinned, singed stubble only).

The boss after pivoting about 80 deg on its planted boot during the growth roar, so it ends facing a hero who broke it from the flank; still wrong: the sun blows out the sky, the knight reads small at this lens.
The boss settling out of its phase-3 growth, chest and glaive squared to the hero's side of the ring; still wrong: flat GL light, soft blotchy trees behind, hero lost behind its legs.

The boss mid-rise from its growth kneel, its right knee now off the ash before the hips heave round onto the hero (fixed-lens pivot sequence); still wrong: the lens sits too far to judge the boot twist, a ring flame blurs into the top-right corner, the sky is flat.

Boss growth rise, leg lens: before (left) the surcoat's front panel jutted off the hip as a stiff red slat pitched to the thigh; after (right) it lies over the knee and falls plumb. Still GL-only lighting, legs dark.
Phase-2 boss after the growth beside the hero, surcoat panel now draped over the knee instead of a diagonal strip; the hero reads small and crouched at the left, trees soft in GL.

The boss in its growth kneel from behind, before (left) vs after (right): the back surcoat panel hangs between the legs and the kneeling boot passes beside it; the bot-measured knee poke through the cloth (~0.2 s) is gone, but the frames look alike and the low lens crops the panel.
Rear leg lens a little later in the rise (st=56): heavy boots on the ash, the panel above frame; dust puffs read flat and the stones are soft in GL.

The boss's guard stance after the growth surge, before (left) vs after (right): the old boots stood nearly heel to heel on one line, the new base sets them apart (ankle gap 0.35 -> 0.89 x the shoulder width) for a heavier, planted giant; GL lighting keeps the legs very dark.

Front leg lens at the phase-2 settle with the wider base: the boss stands square on the ash with its glaive up; the lens aims at the pre-surge spot so the knight sits off-centre, and the stones/trees are soft in GL.
The phase-2 giant turning on the spot on the ring's slope, boots planted on the ash (its pivot ball no longer creeps); low lens crops the body and the armour reads very dark in GL.

Run stop mid-brake (frame 1.60 s): front boot planted heel-first, back boot coming down onto its ball, both on the turf; the lens is behind on near-flat ground and the GL fallback leaves the turf flat and over-saturated, so it doesn't show the downhill fix and would not pass as Wukong.
Run stop settling (frame 1.72 s): the hero squares up over planted boots with no skid; still a GL render from behind, flat ochre ground with sparse leaf decals.
Final-size boss (x4.6) turning on the ring's slope, 10 frames in: pivot boot planted, the other set wide; boots sit in shadow and the low lens crops the body.
Same turn 22 frames in: the outside boot lifts on its ball and swings round with no pop; turf reads as flat mottled dirt at this lens.

Hero's right turn on the spot, settle ticks 48-66: top the old order (boots stacked together until tick 66), bottom the new order (far boot stepped out by tick 54, open stance held); boots still in shadow, lens crops the body.
Left turn settle ticks 30-72 with the new order: the right boot steps wide over ticks 42-54 then holds, no slide; boot-scale lens only, dark turf.

Hero's left turn on the spot, ticks 0-72 every 8, front-lit at 11:00: head leads at tick 8, chest by 16, square by 32, boots planted apart and still from 56 on; the hero stands on a dark trampled patch so sole contact reads only from the lit boot tops.
Right turn on the spot at tick 40, sun-side wide lens: the settle steps wide and holds; grass and the hero are lit but the turf under the boots is dark and the trees read soft in GL.

The final-size boss turning on the spot, new sun-side boot lens at 11:30 (frames 56 and 68): the outside boot lifts heel-up then sets beside the planted one, sabatons now lit; the trampled ring turf under them is still dark and the boots stack from this side.
Final-size boss's turn settle, frames 52 / 62: outer boot set flat, then the short settle step now lifted instead of shuffled; ring turf still dark and flat in GL.
Final-size boss mid-turn on the spot from the low sun-side boot lens: the stepping boot comes round lifted; the lens still crops the body at the hips and stacks the boots.
Same turn after the settle step: both boots planted on the turf where the squared body wants them, no slide; framing and the dark shadow blob in the foreground still need work.
Ashen knight at x3.2 half a second after stopping a walk: both boots planted wide on the turf; the lens sits behind its flank, the foreground is a dark shadow blob and the trees read blotchy.
Same stop 1.8 s later, after the settle steps and the release: the boots have not moved (the creep is gone); framing and lighting still not Wukong-grade.
Crown reel daze, front-lit: left gauntlet cupping the bowed helm, glaive drooped blade-first to the turf, knees buckled; armour reads dark and flat in the GL fallback renderer.

Crown reel impact frame, front-lit for the first time: the glaive is now knocked down across the body with the bowed head instead of standing at guard height; the giant's scale still does not read without the hero in frame.
The surge's coil from the knight's flank: down on its knee, hunched over the glaive as the plate cracks glow; a fallen slab darkens the foreground, and from the front the kneel barely reads.
The Ashen Knight's growth roar, front-lit at hour 9: glaive heaved up, fist raised, helm now thrown back; still small in frame at this distance and the knocked-down hero's pose is stiff.

Ashen Knight growth coil, front-lit: before (straight back, helm up) / after (spine curled, helm sunk between the shoulders) / flank after; the knight is still small in the lens and GL fallback lighting is flat.
The kneeling coil from the flank: back curled over the planted glaive, plate cracks glowing; the frame is wide and the boss small, not yet a Wukong shot.
Helm close-ups, crown-reel shake-off: old toss at 1.13 s (left, face level), new at 1.0 s (mid, still bowed) and 1.13 s (right, tossed back); low-res software render.
The Ashen Knight shaking off a plunge to the helm, front-lit: the helm now tosses back past level (+16 deg); the boss still reads small in this low lens.
Before: the slumped haft ran straight up the chest into the bowed helm's chin skirt (0.15 m/size through it) and the blade hung over the turf.

Ashen Knight's crown reel daze, front-lit: the glaive now angles out from the hip with its blade in the turf, clear of the bowed helm; the boss is still small in the lens and the helm's face never shows.
Crown hit-stop before (left: the glaive pointed at the lens at chest height, its blade edge-on across the throat) vs now (middle, rt 0.09; right, rt 0.14): blade already low and out to the side.
Ashen Knight crown reel, hit-stop frame front-lit at hour 9: the glaive is now knocked down with the head, blade toward the turf; the boss is still small in the lens and the armour reads dark.
Growth-surge heave, helm close-up, before (left) vs after (right): the glaive now rises beside the cracked helm instead of up through it; the GL fallback renderer still flattens the lighting.
Surge kneel from the flank, 2x crop, before (left) vs after (right): the haft's butt no longer rises through the bowed helm and the blade stays in the ash; the boss is still small in this lens.

Reveal opening, side lens: the dormant Ashen Knight leans on its planted glaive, haft now rising past the bowed helm instead of through it; the armour and cape still read flat and blotchy in the GL fallback.
Reveal opening, close lens: the haft now leans out beside the helm with the fist low on it (was running up under the helm); the cape texture is blotchy and the boss lacks fine surface detail.

The hero knocked down by the Ashen Knight's growth blast, now stepped through its real knock-down in the surge shots: lying flat (st=50), back in guard (st=70); the hero is still tiny in this lens and GL lighting is flat.
Phase-2 surge wide: burning ring, knight heaving the glaive with the hero down in front; boss still only ~35% of frame height and backlit armour reads flat.
New close surge lens: the Ashen Knight at its final phase-3 size fills the frame beside the 1.8 m hero; armour still reads flat dark red in the GL fallback renderer.
Close lens early in the growth surge (embers bursting from the helm seams, hero facing it); scale reads, but the knight's plate lacks metal sheen and the frame is GL-only.

The Ashen Knight now reads as fire-blackened steel with leather-bound legs and the oxblood surcoat as its only red (it was one flat dark-red figure); the legs are still near-black blobs with little detail.
Helm before (rust over half the plate), sparse rust only, and final: sparse rust plus a real steel reflectance, so the sun slides over the helm and pauldrons; the plate looks a touch too clean.
The phase-3 giant beside the hero with the new dark steel and leather; the plate now separates from the surcoat, but the GL fallback still lacks SDFGI/SSR and the boots are flat.
Ashen Knight legs, before (left) vs now (right): the blackened leather straps' turns now read through rubbed brown lips with a dull sheen; the shaded leg is still very dark.
Ashen Knight full body in the reveal at 9:00: dark steel plate, red surcoat, strapped legs now show some banding; GL fallback lighting is still flat and the plate a touch clean.

Ashen Knight helm before (top) and after (bottom): soot now runs down the blackened plate in vertical streaks with a few pale ash rivulets, breaking up the clean crown sheen; pauldrons still read clean.
Close reveal frame of the Ashen Knight with streaked plate; the surcoat still reads flat and the GL fallback renderer lacks GI.
Ashen Knight pauldrons before (top) and after (bottom): soot now packs the strip under each lame's rim so the worn-bright rims separate; still subtle, the GL fallback renderer lacks GI.
The Ashen Knight in the ring at hour 9 with sooted plate and pauldrons; legs in shade still read very dark and the scene lacks GI under the GL fallback.

The Ashen Knight's growth roar from the hero's low front view: the helm now stays over the collar with the visor tipped up and the glaive clear of it. Still wrong: the helm reads only as a dark crown with an ember rim, and the plate stays dark in GL.
Before this session: the same roar frame, where the head was flung back behind the gorget, so the giant seemed to have no head from the front.

The Ashen Knight's growth roar from the knocked-down hero's view: the slit's fire now lights the tipped-up visor warm, so the helm reads as a face instead of a black crown; still wrong: GL renderer, the visor detail is soft at this range and the legs are very dark.
Before this session: the same roar frame, the helm a dark crown with only sparks at its rim.

A Hollow Soldier 0.6 s after its walk swung 90 deg toward the lens: body square to its new line, mid-stride on a planted boot (the pace now carries round the corner instead of the walk snapping sideways); still GL fallback lighting, ring floor reads as flat dark dirt.
Ashen Knight's leg straps before (left) and after (right): the lit leather now has a warm brown sheen instead of a grey glaze; the shaded legs still read near-black (GL renderer).
The x3.2 Ashen Knight mid-stride just after a 90 deg corner, on a planted boot with no skid; legs very dark in shade, GL renderer softness.

Ashen Knight intro at 9:00: the shaded leather leg bindings now keep a brown fill so their turns read; still wrong: the plate legs in shade stay near-black and the GL fallback renderer softens everything.
Knight legs 2x crop, before (left) vs after (right): the shaded thigh straps go from a black blob to brown leather turns with dark creases; the shaded greaves are still black.

Hollow Soldier 10 frames after a walk stops, before (left) vs with the new chest sway (right): boots set clean in both; from this near-front lens the forward pitch barely reads, a side lens is still needed to judge it.

Hollow Soldier 6 frames after a walk stops, seen from the new side lens: the chest and hood carry on forward over the front boot, then rock back past upright by frame 72; the soldier still reads a little toy-like in hard sun and the bare ring floor is flat.

Ashen Knight x3.2 after a walk stops: before at f63 (left), with the chest sway at f63 (middle, helm carried forward) and f84 (right, rocked back); the sway reads but subtly, the bladed guard turns this lens 3/4-front, and the shaded leg plate is still near-black.
The x4.6 Ashen Knight striding away after a corner: boots planted and pace carried; the shin bindings read brown, but a bare grey ash knee still shows between the bindings.
The x4.6 knight settled after a stop, side lens: upright with boots planted; still reads small in frame and the knee gap shows grey.

Ashen Knight close-up at 9:00: the thigh straps in the surcoat's cast shadow now read as deep-brown leather turns instead of black blobs; the shins' ash body still reads flat grey and the plate is dark.
The x4.6 Ashen Knight stopping a walk, side lens: the helm carries forward over the front boot with the boots planted; the ring floor still reads flat and the legs dark.
Ashen Knight's knee, before (left: bare grey ash knee between the straps) and after (right: two short leather bindings close it); a small grey wedge still shows behind the bent knee.
x4.6 Ashen Knight striding in the ring with the knees bound; legs still read dark and flat from this backlit angle and the floor reads flat.

Hero climbing the keep from behind mid-reach: the left fist rises beside the hat while the head tips away from it; still wrong: the right hand hides under the capelet, the hair reads as a grey blob and the fist peaks only just over the brim.
3x crop, before (left) vs after (right): the head now leans off the arm reaching overhead so the hat clears the fist; a subtle change, the reach itself still tops out at the brim.
Climb from behind: the reaching right arm reads, but the low left hand is lost behind the mantle and bedroll; the wall's dark masonry and the warm hero read well.
Same frame with the mantle hidden (debug): the left arm is still invisible, so the mantle is not what hides it; the low hand is tucked in front of the chest behind the bedroll.

The hero climbing the keep from behind: the right fist reads up on its stone, the low left hand is still hidden behind the torso and bedroll (traced to the shoulders following the hip sway; no fix shipped yet), and the stone shows speckle noise in the GL fallback.
Hero climbing the keep's outer face, three-quarter from the left: hand-over-hand reads, but the hands hide under the hat brim and capelet and the bedroll fills the back.
Side-on lens of the same climb from above: the reach to the stones reads, the figure is small and the low hand is lost behind the torso.
Running jump at 0.3 s, before (left: legs hanging together) and after (right: push leg trailing, lead knee driven up). Still wrong: both arms held up in a boxer's guard, the hero lit dimly.
Running leap side-on at 0.12 / 0.30 / 0.50 s and 0.03 s into the landing: split stride, lead foot reaching, landing in stride. Still wrong: arms stiff, figure small and in shade.

Running leap side-on at 0.12/0.30/0.45 s: the arms now counter-swing (forward arm reaching ahead, back arm down past the hip) instead of a boxer's guard; the hero is still dim at this lens and the forward hand's fingers splay.
Full frame of the running leap at its rise: the pose reads as a leap, but the backlit hero, flat dark ground and empty yard would not pass as a Wukong shot.
Running leap side-on: the forward hand now closes into a loose half-fist instead of a splayed claw; the hero is still backlit and dim at this lens.
Leap forward hand before (left, fingers splayed and hooked) and after (right, curled into a loose fist); lighting on the hero still too dark.

Standing jump, before/after pairs (rise, apex): the near fist no longer sits up by the chin; arms reach forward and low with loose hands. Still backlit/dim at this lens and the drive frame passes a hand in front of the face.
Standing jump landing 0.06 s in: knees give, arms low and forward, no pop as the arm pose eases out. Lighting flat and the village behind is plain.

Standing jump from the side, old drive frame vs new at 0.10/0.13/0.20 s: the arms now swing up overhead nearly straight and then forward into the tuck instead of a forearm standing up by the face; still backlit and dim at this rear 3/4 lens.
Standing jump at 0.13 s: the near arm thrown up past the hat brim on the drive; the hero is still dark against the shaded cottage and seen from behind.
Standing jump drive (air 0.13 s), front lens with a key light: both arms now thrown up overhead in a V with the face clear; still the flat dirt test spot, and the hero reads small.
Standing jump front-lit: old drive (forearm across the face), new drive 0.10/0.13 s (hands overhead), and 0.20 s, where one hand still passes the mouth on the way into the tuck.
